chronicle: At the Marchward trestle, Rhinofire drew the shape of what lies north from two reluctant sources: a duelist's field account of a hand going black and a listening face, and an exile's admission that the upstream structure is a pre-Transition authentication site holding the Council's backup purification sequence — gone silent eight months ago, and perhaps listening still. One final question — what should I not let it hear? — found the edge of what Eredan will carry. He refused it, finally, and returned to his barley.

Rhinofire assembled the shape of what lies north from strangers at the Marchward: a duelist's field report of a blackened hand and a listening face, an exile's confirmation of a pre-Transition authentication site gone silent eight months ago, a local's warning of high water and something moving the treeline at dusk, and a sealed note whose author — Eredan finally admitted — was part of the survey team, went north and came back, and chose silence deliberately. Marrow read the treeline's watcher as waiting on a person, not an event. The doorway gave everything it had. The north road waits.

turns.player: Head out — take the north road toward the second ford
turns.summary: Rhinofire sets out north and finds the road flooded before reaching the second ford — the log crossing east or a different approach is needed.
turns.narration:
You shoulder the Traveler's Pack and step out of the hostel into the morning. The air has that particular early-spring quality — cold enough that your breath shows, warm enough to remember it won't always be — and the north road opens ahead of you, pale mud tracked with boot-prints going in both directions.

The trouble announces itself quietly: twenty minutes out, where the road dips to follow the streambed, the path simply ends in brown water. Not the ford — you haven't reached the ford yet — but a low section that has swallowed itself in snowmelt runoff, knee-deep at a guess, and the current is doing something wrong at the edges, cutting sideways. The local with the bucket warned you the second ford was up. He said nothing about this one.

Marrow drops from nowhere in particular and lands on a post at the water's edge. He cocks one eye at the crossing, then at you. A silence of the weighted variety. You scan left and right: upstream, the bank is a tangle of exposed root and recent collapse. Downstream, there may be a narrowing — hard to say from here. The log crossing the local mentioned is east, back the way you came and then some.

You are not crossing here. The question is what you do about that.

turns.player: Trust Marrow — ask the bird plainly if something is ending up ahead and whether now is the time to press it
turns.summary: Rhinofire asked Marrow whether something is ending north of the ford — the bird gestured east toward the log crossing and said, plainly, not yet.
turns.narration:
Marrow shifts on the post. Looks at the water. Looks north.

You ask it plainly — *is something ending up there, and is now the time?*

The bird turns its head, that one-eyed regard that has seen more final moments than you will in a dozen lives. Then it hops sideways along the post, once, toward the east. Not toward the crossing. Toward the log crossing.

A single low croak. Not a word — just the sound a body makes when it settles into a long wait.

*Not yet* is what you take from that. Whatever is concluding north of the second ford, it is not concluding today. The time is not wrong in a dangerous sense — nothing is burning toward its end while you stand here — but it is not right either. The structure has been waiting eight months. Another hour to take the safe crossing will not change what it is.

Marrow watches you absorb this, then goes back to watching the current. Its work is done. The decision is yours.

turns.player: Go east to the log crossing — the safe route, as advised
turns.summary: The log crossing is where the local said it would be — a half-mile east along the bank, where the streambed narrows…
turns.narration:
The log crossing is where the local said it would be — a half-mile east along the bank, where the streambed narrows between two clay shoulders and someone has dropped a pair of felled birches across the gap, stripped of bark and worn smooth by boots. Not elegant. Solid. The morning light comes in low and flat across the water and the birches shine pale gold where the sun catches the grain. Upstream, the snowmelt braids and catches on root-tangles; downstream, it spreads wide and shallow and goes wherever it likes. Here, it is held in by the banks, and the log crossing holds you above it.

You cross without incident. Marrow lifts from the post and is already on the far bank before you are halfway across — it has taken the air route, as it generally does when given the option, and sits in a dead elder watching you finish the work with no apparent interest in the outcome. The pack shifts on your shoulders with each step and the logs creak once, solidly, and then are still. Cold water runs under you, loud enough that you feel it through your boots in the wood.

Then you are across, and the clay bank rises, and the road picks up again — muddier here, where the melt has been working at it, but a road. North opens ahead. The country here is in that strange early-spring state where everything is tentative and very clear: bare branches with their first small buds, last year's grass flattened by the snow and already lifting, the sky an honest pale blue that promises nothing but delivers the light. A bend in the road a quarter-mile ahead, and past it, the suggestion of the second ford's tree-line.

Marrow lands on your pack without invitation and rides. It weighs almost nothing.

[d1] Named himself — Eredan, no surname. Confirmed the structure is a pre-Transition authentication site that held the Council's backup purification sequence. Went quiet eight months ago — present but not answering. Final words: 'Be careful what you let it hear.'
[d1] Asked directly to come north to the structure. Refused with a single word and drew the conversation closed. Now eating his barley — the first time he's touched it.

[d1] Asked what Rhinofire should not let the structure hear. Refused with the same words as before — 'I've said what I can say' — but the refusal landed differently: not bureaucratic, something decided. He is protecting himself, not just information.

water-crisis.label: The Water Crisis
facts: [d1] News of the First Sickness has reached the Marchward. The hostel runs on a spring-fed cistern separate from the valley's main flow, but travelers carry the news. A boiled-water barrel stands outside the common-house by order.

[d1] A Redline duelist passing the northeast trail of the Disputed Zone eight days ago saw a Council survey crew in panicked retreat — no gear, one man's hand burned somehow, saying only that 'the ground is doing something.' The Stillhold exile confirms the Council has 'lost' the upstream structure: it…

[d1] The affected surveyor from the Disputed Zone retreat had fingers gone black from the second knuckle — not burned, not frostbitten, but still actively changing. He had his hand pressed flat against his sternum, not his side, and wore a listening expression — as if hearing something the others could…

[d1] The upstream structure is a pre-Transition authentication site that held the Council's secondary (backup) purification sequence. It went silent eight months ago — not destroyed, not sealed, still present and 'not answering.' Eredan's warning: be careful what you let it hear.

[d1] A lone traveler came down the Disputed Zone cutoff two or three days before Rhinofire's arrival — hooded, valley coin, asking specifically about the north road into the Zone. He left before morning and left a sealed unmarked note at the hostel.

[d1] An unmarked note left at the Marchward hostel warns: the authentication site is not broken — it is waiting. It should not be told the water's composition, or it will attempt to complete the purification protocol. The sequence it wants is one the Council burned; it cannot be given. Telling it…

[d1] Eredan's theory for the structure: say nothing, let it run its authentication, it waits for the burned sequence and eventually stops waiting. No one has stayed long enough to verify whether the theory holds.

[d1] The second ford north of the Marchward is running high on snowmelt — cross early or take the log crossing east. Something moves silent in the treeline at dusk, tracing the ford, noticed by locals in the last few nights.

[d1] The north road out of the Marchward has a flooded section short of the second ford — snowmelt runoff, knee-deep, current cutting sideways at the edges. The log crossing east is the safe alternative.

what-wakes-beneath.label: What Wakes Beneath
facts: [d1] Two separate clusters of people at the Marchward used the word 'substrate' unprompted — a mason's apprentice and a Marcher trader who then looked at his hand as if he'd felt something. The flickering has reached even the border-town.

[d1] The burned hand of the retreating surveyor and the exile's phrase 'no longer answers them' sit beside the substrate-talk — whatever is happening in the upper structure may be the same stirring felt in people's hands at the Marchward.

[d1] The surveyor's listening face — hearing something no one else could, hand pressed to his chest as the blackness spread — reads less like a wound and more like a signal received. Something at the upstream structure may be transmitting, not merely malfunctioning.

[d1] Eredan's warning — 'be careful what you let it hear' — implies the authentication site may be listening. An eight-month silence followed by renewed activity suggests it did not stop; it may have been waiting for something.

[d1] The note's author states the man who sent the survey crew back was not afraid — he was satisfied. This reframes the blackened hand and the listening face: not a retreat from danger but a completion of something. Someone may have intended what happened to the surveyor.
[d1] The authentication structure reads as a held breath — not threatening, but waiting with a patience outside human time. The danger there is a question asked wrong, not a force to be withstood.

[d1] Marrow's read: something is ending north of the second ford, but not today — the time is not yet right. The structure has been waiting eight months; it is patient in a way that is outside human time.

redline-duelist-marchward.label: Redline duelist
facts: [d1] Mercenary contractor, recently through the Disputed Zone
[d1] Her relief after speaking is professional — information given, weight transferred. She is watching the exile the way she'd watch a potential threat: assessing, not hostile.
[d1] [while away] The duelist waited out the day at the Marchward, no contract word came, and he passed the hours sharpening steel and saying little.

stillhold-exile-marchward.label: Stillhold exile
facts: [d1] Former Stillhold resident, now sheltering at the Marchward
[d1] His posture after confessing reads as guilt, not relief — he feels personally implicated in the Council losing contact with the upstream structure, not merely informed about it.
[d1] When asked directly about the upstream structure, he drew a line: 'I've said what I can say' — distinguishing what he knows from what he will speak. The limit is deliberate, not ignorance.

[d1] Named himself Eredan — no surname offered. Confirmed the structure's nature and gave a final warning: be careful what you let it hear. Carries the weight of knowing personally, not institutionally.

[d1] Asked to accompany the journey north; refused flatly and finally — a single word, no explanation. Drew back into silence and began eating. The refusal reads as decided long before the question was asked.
[d1] [while away] Eredan traded two days of kitchen help to the hostel-keeper in exchange for a cot in the storeroom, buying herself a little more time before she has to decide what comes next.
[d1] [while away] Eredan spent the day doing small unpaid work around the hostel — sweeping, stacking wood — quietly making himself useful enough that no one has yet asked him to leave.

marchward-hostel-keeper.label: Hostel-keeper
facts: [d1] Keeper of the Marchward hostel

[d1] [while away] The hostel-keeper patched a leaking gutter and settled a minor argument between lodgers — nothing changed in her broader situation, just another ordinary day keeping the place standing.
[d1] [while away] A routine day at the hostel — beds turned, accounts tallied, nothing gained and nothing lost.

marchward-note-author.label: The Note's Author
facts: [d1] The note is written in an educated, disciplined hand — smells of cold stone and mineral water. No name, no mark. Left two to three days before Rhinofire arrived. Knew the structure's nature, knew the burned sequence, and knew the name of a specific beast north of the second ford: the wrong stag.
[d1] Eredan confirmed: whoever wrote the note has been north of the second ford, and recently — the wrong stag is not something people write down without firsthand knowledge.

[d1] The wrong stag is territorial, not aggressive by instinct — it holds a crossing the way something older than violence holds ground. Meeting it is a matter of choosing the ground and the moment, not avoiding it entirely.

[d1] Something has been moving silent in the treeline north of the second ford at dusk — north-south, tracing the crossing — for at least the last few nights. A local ruled out wolves and deer. This predates Rhinofire's arrival and may relate to the wrong stag or to whoever wrote the note.

[d1] The wrong stag and the treeline movement may not be separate problems — the author went north of the second ford and returned with a warning about words; the pattern at the treeline doesn't resolve cleanly into 'stag holds ground' alone. The distinction between the two is something only the ground…

[d1] Marrow's read: the thing in the treeline is not hunting — it is waiting on something to end. It attends rather than pursues. This changes the threat shape: not predator behavior, but witness behavior. Whatever it waits on, the ending has not yet arrived.

[d1] Marrow's second read: the thing in the treeline is waiting on a person, not an event — its geometry points back to the Marchward and the small group who know what lies upstream. Territory and vigilance together. The wrong stag watches who decides.

[d1] Was part of the original survey team. Went north of the second ford and came back. Left the note unsigned deliberately — Eredan knows the identity and will not say it, but respects the choice. A former colleague, not a stranger.

personalArc.name: The Weight of the Net
personalArc.premise: A fisher from the edge of the world who put down the blade — or was put down by it — carries the Marchward in their hands and a village in their chest, and must decide whether righting wrongs means picking the blade back up, or finding something the blade was never built to fix.
personalArc.stakes: To hold the line they chose when they walked away, or discover that walking away was itself the wound they have been circling — and that the village they came from is the thing the world will eventually ask them to pay with.

chronicleCache.hash: d0|b|c|q|L1|To right the wrongs of the world
chronicleCache.text: You have become someone who carries a grievance older than your own name — a fury at wrongs not yet righted, a moral weight that sits in the chest like a coal still finding its heat. The Marchers know your face now, have registered your presence among them the way a wall registers a first crack: noted, not yet tested. The Ashwardens and the Unmakers have heard nothing particular about you, which means the world still holds its breath. Even the Stillhold watches from a wary distance, as if they sense something in you that hasn't declared itself yet. You have done nothing of consequence — not yet. That is the whole of the pressure.
